- To see raw bytes of output when in doubt, pipe through 'od -c' or 'cat -A'.
- Line 4 echoes the exact raw bytes of --c, so line 4 is your microscope for how Python renders a bytes object.
- Run MANY probes (30+). Be systematic and exhaustive. Report ONLY what you actually observed, with the exact command and exact output. Mark anything you infer but did not directly observe as unverified.


YOUR JOB: adversarial verification. Another agent probed area "base58-core" and claims these rules about /workspace/dataset/test20_executable.
Your default assumption is that each rule is WRONG, over-general, or missing an edge case.

For EACH rule below, design and run FRESH commands (do not just repeat their evidence command) that would EXPOSE it if false. Try boundary values, empty values, and combinations. Then judge.

RULES TO ATTACK:
[1] rule: argv is decoded with surrogateescape, so a raw non-UTF-8 byte in --a/--d survives as a lone surrogate and .encode() fails: `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udcNN' in position <i>: surrogates not allowed`, RC=1, no stdout.

'\udcff' in position 0: surrogates not allowed`.
[2] rule: The ENCODE side (--a, --d) performs NO whitespace stripping of any kind — leading, trailing and internal whitespace bytes are encoded literally.
    their evidence: `--a 'trail  '` (74 72 61 69 6c 20 20) -> line1 `b'5QwhXtWus5'` = Node over all 7 bytes. `--a '  '` -> line1 `b'3So'` = Node over 2 space bytes (would be `b''` if stripped). `--a $'\ttab\there'` -> `b'7yqis7Rjvrzp'`. `--a 'a b'` -> `b'ZdBF'`.
[3] rule: Line 12 (enc3) always equals b58encode(b58decode(--b)), i.e. the canonical base58 re-encoding of --b. For every valid canonical base58 --b (including leading '1's) line 12 reproduces --b exactly; when --b had trailing whitespace, line 12 is the rstripped form; when --b is '' or all-whitespace, line 12 is b''. Line 11 (dec_check2) always equals line 2 (dec1).
    their evidence: For all 22 decode vectors tested, line12 == `b'<--b>'` and line11 == line2 (checked programmatically; 0 mismatches). `--b '2 '` -> line12 `b'2'`. `--b '  '` -> line12 `b''`. `--b '11111'+300-char body` -> line12 `b'11111EzHUK8kp6cDim...'`.

    their evidence: `--b 'g'` -> line2 `b"'"` (double-quoted form). `--b '3yj'` -> line2 `b'\'"'` (both quotes present -> single quote with escaped apostrophe). `--b 'zzzzz'` -> `b"'\x1f5\x9f"`. `--a 'back\slash'` decode path -> `b'back\\slash'`. `--b 'A'` -> `b'\t'`, `--b 'C'` -> `b'\x0b'`, `--b 'E'` -> `b'\r'`. A Node reimplementation of exactly this rule matched every observed line 1/2/7/8/11/12.
